newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo wants more African mining spending.
newsitem.headline: Anglo wants more African mining spending.

text.p: African countries had undergone major economic and political reforms in the past 10 years, but governments could do a lot more to lure foreign capital for mining, Anglo American Corp of South Africa said.

Bobby Danchin, chairman of Anglo's new mining business unit, said on Wednesday a recent survey had shown a 12 percent rise in exploration expenditure, but this had not resulted in a commensurate upturn in spending on new mines.
"If one excludes South Africa, the African continent accounts for less than five percent of global expenditure on new mining projects," Danchin told the Investing in African Mining Conference.
He said government implementation of investor-friendly reforms often lagged far behind their good intentions, particularly in the case of mining legislation and the removal of fiscal constraints.

"There has been much talk about the establishment of an environment that encourages the exploitation and exploration of minerals. Here especially implementation lags far behind good intentions," Danchin said.
"For the most part it is true to say that Africa is still uncompetitive on a global basis because of fiscal impositions."

He said governments would stand to gain much from spelling out to interested mining companies fiscal constraints at the outset of exploration. A further drawcard for investment would be favourable tax incentives.

"Governments should be aware of the very considerable amounts of indirect revenue which will be raised from exploration, capital investment and mining operations...The key to attracting mining investment is to provide tax incentives on the various tax charges on mining profits," he said.
